Project

Export/import JSON keeps both Fiddle and REPL code in one project file. Import starts fresh sessions without running code. Terminal output and live definitions are not saved.

Write. Run. Repeat. HTML creates the page, CSS styles it, and ClojureScript brings it to life. Use js/document for DOM access and println for the console. Use the corner button on any pane to maximize it; click Restore or press Escape to return. Use Project → Export JSON to save both modes in a .cljsfiddle.json file. Import JSON restores the code and active mode; Undo import recovers the previous code. In Fiddle mode, Download runnable HTML saves a standalone page with its runtime included. Fiddle runs start fresh. In REPL mode, definitions persist until Restart session. Run file evaluates the whole REPL editor; Alt/Option+Enter or Eval expression runs the selection or top-level expression at the cursor. The terminal accepts expressions with Enter and multiline input with Shift+Enter. Powered by Scittle / SCI: core functions, atoms, and JS interop are available; arbitrary npm/Maven dependencies and full compiler features are not.
ClojureScript editingTab Smart indent · Shift Tab OutdentCtrl / ⌘ + / Toggle commentsCtrl / ⌘ + Shift + I Reindent selection, or all codeAlt / ⌥ + ↑ Select enclosing collection; repeat to expandAlt / ⌥ + ↓ Restore previous selection after expandingUse the Structure menu in either ClojureScript pane to slurp, barf, splice, or wrap complete forms. Ctrl / ⌘ + Alt / ⌥ + ← / → slurps backward/forward; add Shift to barf. With the same modifiers: S splices, P wraps in ( ), V in [ ], and M in { }. Undo with Ctrl/⌘+Z. Brackets and double quotes pair automatically. Select text before typing an opening bracket to wrap it.
